beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed, intrigued]Someone painted ^swimmers, in one of the driest places on ^Earth, where it hardly ever ^rains. [act:vivid, quiet]Little red figures, arms and legs spread wide.
[d:tension][act:the question, leaning in][tune:rise]Were they swimming, or ^dead?

[d:calm][act:storytelling]In {1933|nineteen thirty-three}, the explorer ^Almásy found this cave, in the far south-west of ^Egypt. [act:steady]He called it the Cave of ^Swimmers. [act:light, a small smile]Decades later, the film The English ^Patient made it ^famous.

[d:build][act:impressed, building]In {2002|two thousand two}, a second shelter turned up ^nearby: the Cave of ^Beasts. [p:0.93][act:vivid, painting it]Its painted wall is seventeen metres ^wide, as long as ten people lying head to ^toe. [p:0.9][act:impressed]And on it, five to eight thousand ^figures. [act:vivid, listing them][tune:fall]Hands, ^swimmers, and headless ^beasts.

[d:build][go:3|0][act:explaining, a simple picture]Some of the hands are ^stencils: press something to the rock, blow paint around it, and its outline ^stays. [act:curious, setting it up]A few tiny ones looked like a baby's ^hands. [act:delighted, a little amazed]A closer look showed they were made with the feet of ^lizards.

[d:build][act:fair, even]So what do the swimmers ^mean? [act:fair, the first reading]Almásy thought they showed a real ^lake, from a time when this desert@noun was ^green. [act:the other reading, measured]Many archaeologists see something ^else: the dead, floating in the dark waters that came before ^creation. [p:0.93][act:explaining, careful]In later Egyptian belief, the world rose out of a dark, endless ^ocean. [act:explaining, careful]And that idea, with the dead drifting in those waters, appears in Egyptian ^tombs.

[d:reveal][act:the crux, precise]The paintings date to roughly six and a half to four and a half thousand years ^BCE. [act:fair]The Egyptian texts come two or three thousand years ^later. [p:0.93][act:a picture of time, unhurried]That's like explaining a Roman mosaic with a book written ^today. [p:0.93][act:explaining, fair]Ideas can travel that far in time, but they ^change on the way. [act:plain][tune:fall]A long gap to ^bridge.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, even][tune:rise]Did Egyptian ideas of the afterlife begin in these ^caves? [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*Open ^question*. [act:fair]Possible, but the bridge across all those centuries is still ^missing.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, warm, a small smile][tune:fall]The swimmers aren't telling ^yet.
